purpose: Rules for analysing Cog usage and proposing deterministic improvements without mutating the live library.

rules.description: Requests that initially resolve X are recipe-learning opportunities. Prefer a reusable parameterised recipe when the taught solution succeeded.
A learned recipe reused after teaching is evidence that deterministic learning paid off.
Repeated adjacent successful recipe sequences are candidates for a composite sequence recipe.
Recipes with numbered parameters such as source1/source2 or rigid fixed arity should be reviewed for a more general collection form.
Observed requests matching more than one recipe are candidates for pattern or priority refinement.
Recipes with identical canonical actions may be aliases or merge candidates.
Repeated failed executions should propose a recovery or diagnostic recipe keyed by evidence.
Timed-out executions should propose timeout-aware diagnostic or retry policy recipes rather than blind timeout inflation.
Recipes never selected across a sufficiently large merged usage corpus should be reviewed, not automatically deleted.
Recipes found in merged manual runs but absent from the current library are import candidates; never auto-import without review.
